# Phase 5 — Audit Results, Reporting & Export

**Depends on:** Phases 0–4

**Goal:** Turn the findings generated by the static audit engine into a clear, actionable audit experience. Users must be able to understand the overall state of a Shopify theme, investigate individual findings, trace each Shopify compliance issue back to its requirement/source, and export the results.

This phase does not change how findings are detected. It is responsible for presenting and distributing the results generated by Phases 3 and 4.

## Core principle

The report must clearly distinguish:

```text
Shopify Theme Store Compliance
Accessibility
Technical SEO
Technical AEO
Bug
Internal Standard
```

A general best-practice issue must never be presented as a Shopify Theme Store violation unless its associated requirement is actually a Shopify requirement.

## 1. Audit results data

The reporting layer consumes:

```text
AuditRun
Finding[]
Requirement[]
Rule[]
AuditDiagnostics
```

The report must preserve the relationship:

```text
Finding
  ↓
Rule
  ↓
Requirement
  ↓
Source
```

For Shopify compliance findings, source traceability is mandatory wherever the requirement has an authoritative source reference.

## 2. Audit summary

Create a summary for every completed audit.

Example:

```text
Theme: Adorn
Audit: #104

Overall status
NOT READY

Total findings: 42

Blocker   3
High      12
Medium    18
Low        9
```

Also provide category-level counts:

```text
Shopify Theme Store Compliance   18
Accessibility                     7
Technical SEO                     5
Technical AEO                     4
Bug                               5
Internal Standard                 3
```

The summary must be calculated from actual findings, not manually entered.

## 3. Submission readiness summary

The report should provide an initial readiness status based on configured rules.

Suggested states:

```text
READY
NOT_READY
INCOMPLETE
```

### NOT_READY

Use when one or more findings classified as submission-blocking remain unresolved.

### READY

Use only when all configured mandatory/blocker conditions are satisfied.

### INCOMPLETE

Use when required analysis could not be completed or important requirements do not yet have automated coverage.

This distinction is important.

A theme should not be called:

> "Ready to submit"

when the application simply did not implement enough rules to evaluate it.

## 4. Coverage summary

Show how much of the configured Shopify requirement set is actually automated.

Example:

```text
Shopify requirements

Total:          150
Implemented:    112
Partial:         18
Not implemented: 20

Automated coverage: 74.7%
```

The report should make it clear that:

> A clean audit with 75% rule coverage is not equivalent to a fully validated Shopify submission.

This is especially important during early development.

## 5. Finding list

Create a filterable findings table.

Recommended columns:

```text
Severity
Category
Rule
Finding
File
Line
Confidence
Status
```

Filters:

- Category
- Severity
- Rule
- Requirement
- File
- Confidence
- Finding status

Sorting:

- Severity
- Category
- File
- Line
- Newest
- Status

## 6. Finding status

Findings should support lifecycle status.

Suggested values:

```ts
type FindingStatus =
  | 'open'
  | 'resolved'
  | 'ignored';
```

### Open

The issue is currently present.

### Resolved

The issue was fixed in a later audit or explicitly marked resolved.

### Ignored

The user intentionally excluded the finding.

Ignoring a finding should require a reason in later iterations.

Do not delete findings from the audit history merely because they are resolved.

## 7. Finding detail view

Clicking a finding should open a detailed view containing:

```text
Severity
Category
Finding
Recommendation
File path
Line number
Source snippet
Rule ID
Requirement ID
Confidence
Source/reference
```

Example:

```text
BLOCKER

Missing alt attribute

sections/product-card.liquid
Line 42

<img src="{{ product.featured_image | image_url }}">

Recommendation:
Add an appropriate alt attribute or use an explicitly
decorative empty alt value when the image is decorative.

Rule:
A11Y-IMG-ALT-001

Requirement:
SHOPIFY-A11Y-001

Source:
Shopify Theme Store accessibility requirement
```

## 8. Code context

Where the parser provides source locations, display surrounding source code.

Example:

```text
38  <div class="product-card">
39
40    {% if product.featured_image %}
41      <img
42        src="{{ product.featured_image | image_url }}"
43      >
44    {% endif %}
45
46  </div>
```

The UI should highlight the relevant line.

Do not rely on line numbers alone. File path + rule + finding text should remain the primary identity.

## 9. Source traceability panel

For Shopify compliance findings, show:

```text
Rule
 ↓
Requirement
 ↓
Shopify source
```

Include:

- Requirement ID
- Requirement title
- Requirement description
- Source document
- Source section/reference
- Source URL where available

This allows a developer/reviewer to verify why the finding exists.

## 10. Category dashboards

Provide separate summary views for:

### Shopify Theme Store Compliance

Show:

- Blockers
- High-risk findings
- Open findings
- Requirement coverage
- Rules not yet implemented

### Accessibility

Show:

- Image issues
- Form/label issues
- ARIA issues
- Keyboard/focus structural issues
- HTML language issues

### Technical SEO

Show:

- H1 issues
- Heading hierarchy
- Metadata
- Canonical
- Image structure

### Technical AEO

Show:

- Product schema
- Organization schema
- Article schema
- JSON-LD validity
- Structured-data implementation

### Bugs

Show:

- Broken references
- JavaScript issues
- Configuration issues
- Dependency issues

### Internal Standards

Show:

- Internal UX
- Internal accessibility
- Internal architecture
- Internal performance
- Other configured standards

## 11. Audit diagnostics

Display analysis limitations separately from findings.

Example:

```text
Audit diagnostics

Parser warnings:                 3
Unresolved dynamic references:  14
Rules skipped:                   2
Files skipped:                   0
```

A diagnostic is not automatically a failure.

The UI should make the distinction clear:

```text
Finding:
A confirmed problem.

Diagnostic:
The analyzer could not fully determine something.
```

## 12. Search

Provide global search within an audit.

Search should cover:

- Finding text
- Recommendation
- File path
- Rule ID
- Requirement ID
- Source reference

Do not search raw ZIP contents directly from the report UI unless a future code-browser feature requires it.

## 13. Export formats

The core application should support local exports without requiring external APIs.

### CSV

Export a flat findings table.

Recommended fields:

```text
Audit ID
Theme
Severity
Category
Rule ID
Requirement ID
Finding
Recommendation
File
Line
Confidence
Source
Status
```

### XLSX

Create a structured workbook.

Suggested sheets:

```text
Summary
Findings
Shopify Compliance
Accessibility
Technical SEO
Technical AEO
Bugs
Internal Standards
Rule Coverage
Diagnostics
```

### JSON

Export the complete machine-readable audit result.

Include:

```text
Audit metadata
Summary
Coverage
Findings
Diagnostics
Rule metadata
Requirement references
```

### HTML/PDF

Optional report format for sharing.

The HTML version should be generated locally.

If PDF generation is added, it should use the same report data rather than implementing a separate reporting logic.

## 14. Optional Google Sheets integration

Google Sheets should remain optional.

The application must work completely without Google credentials.

If enabled later:

```text
Audit
 ↓
Export adapter
 ↓
Google Sheets API
 ↓
Spreadsheet
```

Do not make Google Sheets a requirement for completing an audit.

The export layer should use an adapter pattern so other destinations can be added later.

Example:

```ts
interface ReportExporter {
  export(report: AuditReport): Promise<ExportResult>;
}
```

Implement:

```text
CsvExporter
XlsxExporter
JsonExporter
HtmlExporter
GoogleSheetsExporter (optional)
```

## 15. Report generation model

Create a normalized `AuditReport` object.

Suggested structure:

```ts
type AuditReport = {
  auditRun: AuditRun;

  theme: {
    id: string;
    name: string;
  };

  summary: {
    overallStatus: 'READY' | 'NOT_READY' | 'INCOMPLETE';
    totalFindings: number;
    blocker: number;
    high: number;
    medium: number;
    low: number;
    byCategory: Record<string, number>;
  };

  coverage: {
    totalRequirements: number;
    implemented: number;
    partial: number;
    notImplemented: number;
    percentage: number;
  };

  findings: Finding[];

  diagnostics: AuditDiagnostic[];

  generatedAt: Date;
};
```

All UI and export formats should consume this normalized representation.

## 16. Report snapshots

When an audit is completed, store enough information to reproduce the report even if rules change later.

At minimum, preserve:

- Audit run metadata
- Finding data
- Rule IDs
- Requirement IDs
- Severity
- Source references
- Parser/rule version information where available

Do not recompute historical reports solely from today's rule definitions.

## 17. Rule/version information

Include versions where possible:

```text
Audit:
2026-08-12

Rule engine:
1.0.0

Parser:
1.0.0
```

This will become important when Shopify requirements or rule implementations change.

## 18. UX requirements

The report should make the most important issues immediately visible.

### Primary hierarchy

```text
Overall readiness
 ↓
Blockers
 ↓
High severity
 ↓
Category breakdown
 ↓
Individual findings
 ↓
Source/rule details
```

Do not overwhelm the user with hundreds of low-priority issues before showing blockers.

## 19. Empty and incomplete states

Handle:

### No findings

```text
No issues detected by the currently enabled rules.
```

Do not say:

```text
Shopify approved.
```

The application is an auditor, not Shopify.

### Incomplete coverage

Clearly show:

```text
Audit incomplete

20 Shopify requirements currently have no automated rule.
```

### Parser limitation

Clearly show:

```text
Some dynamic theme behavior could not be statically verified.
```

## 20. Audit comparison preparation

Phase 5 should prepare the report model for the future re-audit/diff phase.

Findings should retain stable identifiers:

```text
ruleId
category
filePath
finding
```

Do not use line number as the only identity because line numbers can change between theme versions.

## 21. Acceptance criteria

Phase 5 is complete when:

- Completed audits have a usable summary dashboard.
- Findings can be filtered and sorted.
- Finding details show file, line, source context, severity, rule, and requirement.
- Shopify compliance findings provide source traceability.
- Category summaries are available.
- Submission readiness can be displayed as READY, NOT_READY, or INCOMPLETE based on configured rules/coverage.
- Rule coverage is visible.
- Audit diagnostics are visible separately from findings.
- CSV export works locally.
- XLSX export works locally.
- JSON export works locally.
- HTML export works locally.
- PDF export can be generated if included in the implementation.
- Google Sheets is optional and does not block the core audit.
- Historical audit data remains available.
- Reports are generated from a normalized `AuditReport` model.
- No AI API is required.
- No Voyage API is required.
- No vector database is required.

## Explicitly out of scope

Do not build:

- AI/LLM review
- Voyage
- Embeddings
- Vector search
- RAG
- Re-audit comparison logic
- Automated finding lifecycle across multiple audits
- Shopify submission API integration
- Automatic Shopify submission
- Browser-based runtime auditing
